label: The arrangement carries competition-law risk
definition: The agreement contains a vertical restraint — exclusive supply or distribution, tie-in, refusal to deal, or resale price maintenance — which is void under the Competition Act if it causes an appreciable adverse effect on competition. The instrument must state the restraint's business justification and preserve the distributor's pricing freedom.

authority.note: Vertical agreements: tie-in, exclusive supply, exclusive distribution, refusal to deal, resale price maintenance — void if they cause an appreciable adverse effect on competition.
The factors by which appreciable adverse effect is assessed.
Agreements in restraint of trade are void, subject to the sale-of-goodwill exception.

sets_resale_price.note: Resale price maintenance is the highest-risk restraint of the set and should never be drafted as a fixed price without a justification.

confirmation.question: Will the distributor be the only one allowed to sell in this territory?
confirmation.why: Exclusive arrangements are lawful but can be struck down if they shut competitors out of the market, so the agreement should record why the exclusivity is commercially justified.
options: Only the manufacturer may also sell

unresolved_behaviour.safe_default_note: Draft the non-exclusive appointment. Exclusivity is the restraint; its absence carries no competition risk.
unresolved_behaviour.rationale: The asymmetry is clear: a non-exclusive appointment where the parties intended exclusivity is a commercial gap the parties will notice and correct, whereas an exclusivity term they did not intend is a void restraint they will not notice until it is litigated.

authoring_note: This concept exists today entirely inside generationControls as include_competition_compliance, with no statutory citation attached to it anywhere. Making it a concept is what gives that determination an authority list.
